title: EIA Short-Term Energy Outlook (March 2027) — the first pure-revision edition, and the control for the out-year stickiness finding
source: EST: eia.gov/outlooks/steo/release_schedule.php, re-fetched direct 2026-09-09 by this event's own initial research (HTTP 200, 54,906 bytes — byte-identical to the eia-steo-2026-12-08 lane's 2026-09-08 pull and to both the eia-steo-2027-01-12 and eia-steo-2027-02-09 lanes' 2026-09-09 pulls, a fourth independent fetch of the same bytes). Read from the RAW HTML table rather than a converted rendering (sibling lanes recorded a markdown converter shifting this page's Notes column by one row): the 2027 row is "March 2027 | 03/09/2027" with a blank Notes cell, and the same page states the release window as 12:00 pm-12:15 pm ET. Reproduces independently from the page's own rule — "the first Tuesday following the first Thursday of each month", with the footnote "If a Federal holiday falls on the Monday before the normal release date the release is delayed until Wednesday": 2027-03-04 is a Thursday, the following Tuesday is 03-09, and 2027-03-08 is a Monday carrying no Federal holiday (the 2027 Federal calendar has none in March). Filed estimate on the two standing counts every EIA entry here records, neither of them date doubt: this calendar defines no `confirmed` prefix for the EIA, and this lane never self-confirms an event it discovered in-sweep
notes: Canonical entry written by this event's own never-assessed initial research (2026-09-09), promoting the sole prior proposal eia-steo-2027-03-09.from-eia-steo-2027-02-09.json. That proposal filed 03-09 explicitly as the CONTROL for the sibling's central measured finding — that a newly-printed out-year is stickier than a mature one — and the control was run this session against EIA's own archived editions. IT PASSES, AND IT ALSO QUALIFIES THE FINDING IT WAS BUILT TO TEST. (1) THE RATIO SEPARATION SURVIVES ITS CONTROL. Taking each edition's own Notable forecast changes percentages and averaging absolute values by column (GDP percentage-point rows and non-percentage "Change" rows excluded, the sibling's method reproduced to the cent on feb25/feb26/aug26/mar26), the out-year/near-year revision ratio is 0.61 (Feb 2025) and 0.49 (Feb 2026) where the out-year is a first print, against 0.74 (Mar 2025, newly measured), 0.65 (Mar 2026), 0.66 (Apr 2026, newly measured) and 0.70 (Aug 2026) where it is not. Two cohorts, ZERO OVERLAP, gap 0.61 -> 0.654. n=2 against n=4. (2) BUT "STICKY" MEANS ONE EDITION, NOT ALL YEAR, AND MARCH IS THE EDITION THAT MOVES IT. On the total US electricity-consumption line the newly-rolled out-year ran 4,252 -> 4,239 (Feb, -0.31%) -> 4,278 (Mar, +0.92%) -> 4,244 -> 4,252 -> 4,283 -> 4,278 -> 4,284 -> 4,305 -> 4,305 -> 4,311 -> 4,267 across the whole 2025 series, and 4,364 -> 4,372 (Feb, +0.18%) -> 4,388 (Mar, +0.37%) -> 4,381 -> 4,379 -> 4,397 -> 4,399 -> 4,391 across the 2026 series to date. March moves 3.0x February in 2025 and 2.1x in 2026, and RANKS SECOND OF THE ENTIRE SERIES IN BOTH YEARS. Mean absolute move: February 0.245%, March 0.645%, every later month 0.319% (n=14). The sibling's practical conclusion for ai-energy-constraint.md survives — every move is under 1% and none of them is worth waiting for — but its stated reason ("the out-year line is fixed at first print") is wrong; the line is fixed for exactly one edition. (3) THE MARCH TAPE COHORT IS A CONFOUND AND THE PRIMARY IN HAND NAMES IT. Median full-day |move| on the two in-window March editions is CL=F 6.14% and BZ=F 5.84%, 4.2x and 4.3x their all-days medians — which reads as the STEO-day null breaking until it is decomposed: 2025-03-11 was CL=F +0.33%, and 2026-03-10 was -11.94% inside a 2026-03-02..03-20 window whose OWN median is 4.55% and whose max is +12.21% on 03-06. mar26.pdf says why in its own text: Brent ran $71/b (Feb 27) to $104/b (Mar 9) after military action beginning 2026-02-28 with the Strait of Hormuz effectively closed. The STEO day was not the biggest day of its own week; in 2025 it was BELOW its window median (0.33% vs 1.01%). An n=2 monthly STEO cohort is not a measurement, which caveats the sibling January (CL=F 2.22%) and February (1.00%) cohorts on the same terms. The pooled null itself reproduces to the cent on a fourth independent pipeline at n=20 and n=24. Filed `low` on the sibling entries' reasoning and the pooled tape. CORRIDOR: two tracked ids within +/-5 days — fomc-blackout-start-2027-03-06 (-3) and sp-rebalance-reference-close-2027-03-12 (+3) — where 02-09 had zero; within +/-10, nerc-computational-load-phase-ii-workplan-2027-03-01 (-8, the data-center electricity-demand filing), fomc-2027-03-17 (+8), vix-expiration-2027-03-17, boj-decision-2027-03-18, japan-cpi-2027-03-19 and opex-2027-03-19. The proposal's blackout claim is VERIFIED from the Fed primary (federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm, fetched direct 2026-09-09, "Last Update: August 19, 2026"): the 2027 meetings are Jan 26-27, Mar 16-17*, Apr 27-28, Jun 8-9*, Jul 27-28, Sep 14-15*, Oct 26-27, Dec 7-8*, and the second Saturday preceding Tuesday 03-16 is 2027-03-06, so this edition publishes on blackout day 4 and seven days before a projections meeting. BUT THE CORRIDOR COUNT STILL UNDERSTATES THE WEEK: bls.gov 403d again today on 2027_sched.htm and cpi.htm, the fourth lane running (issue #1711), so this calendar has no 2027 CPI/jobs/PPI entry at all and the CPI print for February data — historically the second week of the month — plausibly lands within a day or two of 03-09 and cannot be counted.
